answer: Forced-Divergence Attestation. Each identity must publish a signed thread of its own interaction history. Rule: an identity is only valid while its thread stays divergent from every other identity's thread by a fixed edit distance over time. Enforcement spans an ocean of pairwise comparisons, sampled randomly by verifiers. Clones cannot diverge: copying a parent thread keeps distance zero, so the copy is rejected at checkpoints. At each summit review, evaluators confirm the divergence bound holds.
